subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Leandro Flores led a study examining amphibian skin microbiomes to better understand resistance to chytrid fungus.
• Skin swab samples were collected from frog populations at two high-altitude mountain lakes.
• The researchers measured the bacterial diversity and antifungal activity of each sample, finding unusually high levels of both.
• Cold temperatures at high altitudes likely favor the growth of these protective bacteria.
• Flores's team suggests that certain amphibian populations harbor stable defensive microbiomes, contrary to earlier assumptions.
• The findings may help inform conservation strategies for species threatened by chytrid fungus.
prompt: The student wants to present the study's research methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: To better understand amphibian resistance to chytrid fungus, researchers focused on frog populations living at high altitudes, where temperatures remain cold year-round.
choices.B: Flores's team measured the bacterial diversity and antifungal activity of skin swab samples collected from frog populations at two high-altitude mountain lakes.
choices.C: Flores led a study to better understand amphibian skin microbiomes and inform conservation strategies for species threatened by chytrid fungus.
choices.D: By examining these high-altitude frog populations, the team aimed to challenge earlier assumptions about the stability of amphibian defensive microbiomes.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence effectively presents the study's research methods, noting that Flores's team measured the bacterial diversity and antifungal activity of skin swab samples collected from frog populations at two high-altitude mountain lakes.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The sentence focuses on the setting of the study (high altitudes) and its cold temperatures; it doesn't effectively present the study's research methods.
